source.title: Corpus Complexity Matters in Pretraining Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The study compares downstream GLUE performance at different pretraining checkpoints, a different measurement relevant to downstream performance versus training scale; it does not measure scaling-law loss.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports corpus complexity metrics and corpus-to-task similarity correlations. Those results do not measure any other listed claim version. The GLUE results are presented as an average across eight tasks.
record.test_reason: The study is about how corpus complexity affects downstream GLUE scores at a fixed ~100M-token budget. It cites Kaplan et al. only as motivation. Training steps vary only incidentally: three checkpoints (10K/20K/30K, batch size 8) of one BERT-base size, a factor of 3 early in training. There are no loss curves, no model-size variation and no fits. That cannot show whether downstream performance improves predictably with scale, so no version is tested. The checkpoint trends are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that a more complex, lexically diverse corpus correlates with greater vocabulary overlap with GLUE data and better downstream scores, and wikibooks is best at all checkpoints. They also note that longer training does not always raise performance monotonically (books-easy, books-small). They flag that the models and corpora are small.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies the composition and complexity of pretraining corpora and evaluates fine-tuned GLUE performance; it does not fit or test the original scaling-law losses or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported training-progress trend differs by pretraining corpus: books-easy and books-small move opposite to the other three corpora.

fits_no_version.finding: Average GLUE score rises from 10K to 30K pretraining steps for wiki, books-hard and wikibooks, but falls for books-easy and books-small. BERT-base, batch size 8, ~100M-token corpora, figure-only values, no uncertainty.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Over short early-training ranges, the direction of downstream improvement with training steps depends on pretraining-corpus complexity.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed token budget, the corpus with the most types and highest TTR (wikibooks) outperforms the others at all three checkpoints. Complexity correlates with vocabulary overlap and with performance (Kendall's tau, Fig. 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data composition, not only data quantity, shifts downstream performance at fixed pretraining budget.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of The Fourth Workshop on Simple and Efficient Natural Language Processing (SustaiNLP), 2023
record.problems: The GLUE scores in Figure 2 are not numerically available in the text, and no uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper notes that its models and corpora are relatively small and its study is limited to English and generic domains.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for the listed versions. Corpus-characteristic results in Table 1 and similarity/correlation analyses in Figures 3–5 were not included because they do not measure the listed scaling-law versions.

untested.parts: Model-size scaling, loss-to-downstream mapping, any functional form or predictability across orders of magnitude.
No power-law fits for repeated data or fine-tuning.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2/tests classification and the V6 supports/challenges labels are rejected. The step range is too narrow (factor 3, one model size, ~1 epoch) to bear on downstream predictability with scale. Per-checkpoint rows also misrepresent what are trend statements.

versions.untested_parts: Tests downstream GLUE performance across training-step checkpoints only. It does not test model-size scaling, pretraining-loss predictability, or whether performance follows a power law.

rows.subject: BERT-base (uncased)
rows.stage_stated: pretrained from scratch; checkpoints fine-tuned for two epochs
rows.operation_detail: Compare average GLUE performance at pretraining checkpoints.
rows.measure: Unweighted average score across eight GLUE tasks
rows.note: The text says performance increasingly improves with training for wiki, as part of the three-corpus group wiki, books-hard, and wikibooks; exact plotted score is unavailable in the text.
rows.check: A single checkpoint cannot show a trend, and the value is figure-only. The wiki trend across 10K–30K rises, but the factor-3 step range from one run does not bear on V6's predictability with scale.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: wiki, books-hard, and wikibooks across 10K, 20K, and 30K pretraining steps
reader_labels.reason: The authors report increasing average GLUE performance with training for these three corpora (R1–R3, R7–R9, R13–R15).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: books-easy and books-small across 10K, 20K, and 30K pretraining steps
reader_labels.reason: The authors report the opposite training-progress trend for these two corpora, rather than increasing average GLUE performance (R4–R6, R10–R12).
